historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Dopamine precursors

starting.description: DOPA reversed the reserpine-induced animal syndrome and restored brain dopamine; after the discovery of severe striatal dopamine deficit in human Parkinsonian brains, Hornykiewicz explicitly conceived L-DOPA as a means to replace the missing dopamine. A later clinical-development branch also investigated observed pigment loss and its possible relation to biogenic-amine loss.

inspiration.description: Reserpine-induced depletion and its reversal in animals and deficient striatal dopamine in Parkinsonian human brains; dopamine was the endogenous target and L-DOPA its precursor. The later Cotzias branch involved neuromelanin loss, its possible relation to amines, and proposed restoration.

steps.description: A precursor reversed reserpine-induced motor suppression in animals; its effect was correlated with restoration of dopamine in brain. A second retrospective also credits Holtz with an antireserpine DOPA report in 1957.
Carlsson's group linked these results and basal-ganglia dopamine distribution to the idea of dopamine replacement for parkinsonism.
Hornykiewicz and Ehringer detected severe striatal dopamine loss in Parkinsonian autopsy samples, which Hornykiewicz identifies as the basis for proposing L-DOPA replacement.
Hornykiewicz and neurologist Birkmayer translated the idea into an acute intravenous L-DOPA trial in 1961, observing rapid relief of akinesia.

Carlsson also describes early Japanese work by Sano on low brain dopamine and intravenous DL-DOPA, and Canadian work involving oral L-DOPA; these reports should not be collapsed into an exclusively Vienna history.

Cotzias and coauthors' accessible 1967 opening linked pigment and amine deficits through a shared DOPA precursor. A later review characterizes the program as investigating neuromelanin restoration and describes use of DL-DOPA among other agents.

The 1969 report described gradual oral L-DOPA escalation and improvement in a series of 28 patients; a historical review places this after the earlier DL-DOPA work and describes the change to the L form.

design.description: Researchers deliberately selected a catecholamine precursor to reach brain, tested replacement intravenously, and later developed a gradual oral regimen and treatment with the L form rather than the racemic mixture. These are clinical and stereochemical choices, not a claim of de novo molecular design.

circumstances.description: The animal precursor experiment and the clinical replacement test were planned stages; this is not a blanket account of every finding.

limits: The animal experiment illustrated in the Carlsson account used DL-DOPA; the human Vienna trial used L-DOPA. Hornykiewicz also credits Holtz with an antireserpine DOPA report in 1957; that original has not been read.
Carlsson reports early Sano and Canadian contributions as well as Vienna work; primary reports and precise priority are not adjudicated here.
A later neuromelanin-oriented DL-DOPA program contributed to oral development; this does not make it a separate modern drug class.
The 1964 trial abstract does not specify stereoisomer; later summaries differ on at least the oral preparation and are not resolved here.
conflicts: The Vienna collaborators reported striking acute responses (E5), whereas McGeer and Zeldowicz reported objective improvement in only two of ten patients and insufficient benefit in their study (E11); the historical review describes little active–placebo difference in controlled trials (E8). Dose and duration are possible explanations, not established causes of the divergence here.

The later review emphasizes Cotzias's neuromelanin-restoration hypothesis (E6), while his 1967 opening explicitly discusses both pigment and biogenic-amine deficits (E10). Neither establishes that he ignored dopamine or that the two rationales were mutually exclusive.
gaps: The full methods and results of the 1967 and 1969 NEJM clinical papers were not read; the 1967 report was available as an opening excerpt and the 1969 report as the publisher's abstract.

The 1957 animal experiment, 1960 human-brain reports, Sano's 1960 Japanese paper, and the 1961 Vienna clinical paper were not read in full; the observations are supported by retrospective sources as identified.
The 1964 McGeer study was read as an abstract only, so the conflicting secondary descriptions of its stereochemistry could not be settled.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Cotzias used gradual dose escalation to address observed side effects and establish a practical oral levodopa regimen.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: The earlier replacement hypothesis also depended on animal studies and human postmortem biochemistry.
